objectives.wording: Identify lesion types, grade severity and elicit risk factors in a sample case.
Develop a severity-based plan covering scarring risk and follow-up.
Differentiate vitiligo from other hypopigmented lesions and propose a plan.
Distinguish psoriasis from mimics using morphology, distribution and nail findings.
Demonstrate grattage on approved teaching material and explain the finding and its limits.
Discuss chronicity and compare management options with a simulated patient.
Recognize characteristic lesions and outline assessment and management.
Plan treatment, contact management and counselling about adverse effects.
Compare presentation, transmission and management in adults and children.
Prepare and examine approved scrapings on KOH mount and distinguish yeast from dermatophyte findings.
Use a simulated case to choose testing and management by site and extent.
Compare representative adult and paediatric infections by agent, pathogenesis, appearance and management.
Distinguish herpes simplex and herpes labialis from mimics using lesion pattern and recurrence.
Distinguish dermatomal zoster and generalized varicella from other vesicular eruptions.
Identify common wart patterns and distinguish representative mimics.
Identify typical lesions and distinguish them from other papular eruptions.
Relate epidemiology, skin and nerve findings to clinical and operational classifications.
Demonstrate sensory, motor and peripheral nerve assessment in simulation.
Use national and WHO guidance to justify classification, treatment and follow-up in a simulated case.
Assess disability and demonstrate counselling on self-care and stigma.
Explain indications and document observations from a supervised demonstration.
Distinguish reaction types and justify a simulated plan that addresses nerve injury risk.
Explain the rationale and limitations and apply the appropriate pathway to a sample case.
Elicit a nonjudgmental sexual history and demonstrate safer-sex and pretest HIV counselling.
Match clinical stages to findings and interpret representative treponemal and nontreponemal results.
Use findings and serology to justify simulated care and referral, including pregnancy and neonatal scenarios.
Differentiate chancroid and genital herpes and select appropriate diagnostic tests.
Demonstrate consent-based examination with privacy, confidentiality and a chaperone in simulation.
Recognize distinguishing findings and justify management using the applicable syndromic pathway.
Compare gonococcal and nongonococcal causes by presentation, testing and management principles.
Apply the relevant pathway in simulation and counsel on prevention and partner care.
Distinguish likely causes and justify assessment, management and follow-up using the applicable pathway.
Recognize typical lesions and demonstrate discussion of treatment options, prevention and follow-up.
Use clinical findings and targeted tests to assess representative HIV-associated dermatoses.
Recognise representative cutaneous reactions to antiretroviral drugs and justify initial assessment.
Distinguish endogenous and exogenous eczema patterns using exposure history and distribution.
Build a simulated plan and explain topical and systemic options and referral criteria.
Recognize erythroderma and complications and demonstrate stabilization and referral priorities in simulation.
Distinguish fixed drug eruption, drug hypersensitivity and SJS/TEN using morphology, timing and systemic features.
Assess a simulated reaction, prioritize safety and explain documentation and escalation.
Differentiate pemphigus and bullous pemphigoid using clinical findings and explain how Nikolsky and bulla spread signs inform assessment.
Demonstrate assessment and supportive care priorities and arrange referral in simulation.
Classify presentations and explain mechanisms and representative triggers.
Distinguish wheals and angioedema from mimics, assess airway risk and justify initial care in simulation.
Demonstrate elicitation in an appropriate teaching setting and document the response.
Identify representative presentations and distinguish superficial from deeper infections.
Recognize findings in a sample case that warrant surgical assessment.
Compare indications and adverse effects of topical and systemic antibacterial agents used for pyoderma.
Prioritize triage, prehospital handover and emergency primary survey in a trauma scenario.
Distinguish shock mechanisms and justify investigations and initial management priorities.
Compare mechanisms, findings and investigations and demonstrate assessment and initial care in simulation.
Compare shoulder, knee, hip and finger dislocations by mechanism, examination, imaging and management priorities.
Participate in supervised or simulated reductions and document neurovascular findings before and after.
Critically compare recent advances in trauma, sports injuries, arthroplasty and spine care using dated evidence.
Interpret mechanism, examination and imaging in a case and justify management.
Use a simulated case to assess neurovascular status, interpret imaging and justify management.
Choose and communicate an appropriate analgesic plan for a simulated patient with joint pain.
Compare mechanisms and imaging and explain how neurovascular deficits affect management.
Distinguish both-bone, Galeazzi and Monteggia injuries using imaging and explain management principles.
Relate mechanism and radiographic alignment to examination and management.
Interpret a simulated presentation and prioritize haemodynamic assessment, imaging and management.
Connect mechanism and neurological findings to investigations, stabilization and safe mobilization.
Compare patellar, distal femoral and proximal tibial fractures and prioritize neurovascular and compartment assessment.
Compare presentation and management across age groups and recognize and outline initial management of fat embolism syndrome.
Differentiate tibia and fibula, calcaneal, small foot bone and Lisfranc injuries by examination, imaging and management.
Relate injury mechanism and imaging to stability, clinical assessment and management.
Select and interpret investigations for malunion, nonunion and infection in supplied cases.
Recognize an open fracture and explain investigation, initial care and secondary infection prevention.

Describe the mechanism, features, investigation and management of paediatric injuries: supracondylar humeral fracture with neurovascular injury and compartment syndrome, forearm and distal radius fractures, pulled elbow, physeal injuries, and femoral shaft, tibial and both-bone leg fractures; recognize features suggesting non-accidental injury that require safeguarding referral.
Distinguish acute, subacute and chronic osteomyelitis and justify investigation and management.
Demonstrate an assigned team role in simulated abscess drainage, sequestrectomy or saucerization, and arthrotomy.
Distinguish septic arthritis from osteomyelitis and justify investigation and management.
Assist with supervised or simulated aspiration and document preparation, specimen handling and aftercare.
Compare hip, knee and spinal presentations, including cold abscess, and justify investigations and management principles.
Use joint pattern, extra-articular findings and investigations to differentiate rheumatoid, axial spondyloarthritis and psoriatic presentations.
Classify low back pain causes and compare cervical and lumbar spondylosis and disc prolapse by findings, tests and management principles.
Explain the causes, findings, investigation and management of osteoporosis.
Compare osteomalacia and rickets by cause, findings, investigation and management.
Compare Paget disease of bone with other metabolic bone disorders by findings and management.
Assess pattern and functional impact in a case and justify rehabilitation and orthopaedic options.
Assess movement, contractures and function and explain a multidisciplinary orthopaedic plan.
Distinguish representative benign and malignant presentations and outline imaging, referral and fracture management principles.
Localize radial, ulnar, median, common fibular and sciatic deficits, outline assessment and management, and demonstrate splints for foot drop, wrist drop and claw hand.
Compare scoliosis, spina bifida, developmental hip dysplasia, torticollis and clubfoot by presentation, assessment and management principles.
Demonstrate above-elbow, below-knee and above-knee casts, Thomas splint, long-bone splinting and shoulder or clavicle strapping in simulation.
Demonstrate assigned roles in simulated peripheral and central access, catheterization, intubation and splintage.
Explain expected recovery, uncertainty and rehabilitation in simulated fracture, tumour and congenital disability cases.
Recognize warning signs in infection, neurovascular injury and back pain and explain the urgency of higher-centre referral.
Counsel a simulated patient on benefits, risks, alternatives and consent for an orthopaedic procedure.
Apply consent, confidentiality and benefit-risk principles to a simulated anaesthesia case.
Compare lower-limb amputation levels and relate residual limb characteristics and prosthesis choice to below-knee rehabilitation.
Compare contemporary diagnostic groupings with historical neurotic, psychotic, organic and functional distinctions.
Elicit symptoms, timeline, functioning, risk, substance use and relevant collateral history in simulation.
Perform a structured simulated examination and document observed findings separately from reported symptoms.
Recognize presentations involving alcohol, nicotine and locally relevant substances and justify assessment and management pathways in sample cases.
Use a simulated presentation to distinguish psychosis from mimics and justify initial care and referral.
Assess a simulated patient for depression, impairment and safety concerns and develop a follow-up plan.
Identify urgent risk or severe features in a simulated case and communicate the referral.
Recognize a manic episode in simulation and prioritize safety, initial assessment and referral.
Differentiate representative anxiety disorders and demonstrate initial assessment and management planning.
Distinguish acute stress and adjustment disorders in a simulated case and justify referral when indicated.
Describe representative sexual dysfunctions and distinguish symptoms, distress and contextual contributors.
Classify common disorders and compare developmental history and presentation in ADHD and autism.
Explain how intellectual and adaptive functioning inform assessment and support planning.
Demonstrate direct, empathetic assessment of suicidal thoughts, intent, plans and protective factors and identify immediate safety needs.
Describe assessment, consent, anaesthesia, monitoring and recovery and address common misconceptions.
Trace milestones that made anaesthesia a modern specialty.
Map anaesthesiology roles across perioperative care, critical care, pain, labour analgesia and resuscitation.
Compare training and practice roles within the specialty.
Explain indications and demonstrate age-appropriate basic life support in adult, child and neonatal simulations.
Demonstrate adult and paediatric advanced life support in simulation using approved algorithms and team roles.
Outline risk assessment, optimization and communication before surgery.
Elicit, present and document relevant medical, medication and anaesthetic history in simulation.
Perform and document a focused examination including airway and cardiopulmonary assessment.
Select and interpret tests based on patient factors and the proposed operation.
Integrate assessment findings and justify proceeding, optimizing or escalating a simulated case.
Write and justify a simulated prescription that accounts for risks and contraindications.
Compare intravenous and inhaled agents, opioid and non-opioid analgesics, neuromuscular blockers and anticholinesterases by action and relevant adverse effects.
Identify landmarks and explain how anatomy informs airway assessment and device selection.
Observe or review a demonstration and describe preparation, induction and maintenance checkpoints.
Observe a perioperative demonstration and explain measures used to maintain ventilation, circulation and temperature.
Observe monitor setup and explain the purpose and interpretation of representative readings.
Describe observed selection, recovery and discharge safeguards for ambulatory surgery.
Explain observed preparation, monitoring, emergency access and recovery arrangements outside theatre.
Compare indications, principles and limitations of spinal, epidural and combined techniques.
Identify brachial plexus, subarachnoid and epidural landmarks on diagrams or models.
Observe a demonstration and explain preparation, localization, monitoring and safety checks.
Describe an observed demonstration and compare adult and paediatric anatomical and procedural considerations.
Observe representative blocks including brachial plexus approaches and explain their targets and steps.
Outline recovery assessment and resuscitation priorities in a simulated deterioration.
Identify observed crash cart contents and explain the use of key recovery equipment.
Recognize representative postoperative complications and justify initial assessment and escalation.
Use an ICU visit or equivalent observation to describe staffing, monitoring and organ support functions.
Apply representative admission and step-down criteria to simulated cases.
Explain observed monitoring choices and relate trends to organ function.
Describe an observed or simulated structured assessment and stabilization of an unconscious patient.
Observe setup and explain circuit checks, initial settings and alarm verification.
Explain major settings and demonstrate how changes affect ventilation and oxygenation in simulation.
Trace nociceptive pathways and explain modulation and sensitization.
Elicit location, intensity, quality, tolerance and functional effect from a simulated patient or surrogate.
Compare representative agents by target, clinical role and adverse effects.
Explain how assessment, goals and treatment burden inform multimodal pain care.
Use a simulated case to discuss symptom relief, reassessment and patient preferences near the end of life.
Demonstrate peripheral cannulation and safe disposal in simulation.
Demonstrate preparation and central venous access on a task trainer with supervision.
Explain how clinical findings and procedure context guide fluid selection and reassessment.
Match blood components to representative indications and explain preoperative checks.
Relate common surgical positions to pressure, nerve and cardiopulmonary risks.
Identify representative hazards and explain corresponding prevention measures.
Explain how briefings, closed-loop communication and handovers prevent errors.
Classify representative medical and medication errors and identify prevention and reporting steps.
Select and demonstrate setup of nasal cannula, simple mask, Venturi mask, non-rebreather, bag-mask and high-flow nasal oxygen in simulation.
Demonstrate adjustment of flow and inspired oxygen and explain monitoring and safety checks.
Demonstrate head tilt, chin lift and jaw thrust on a simulator and explain selection.
Demonstrate selection, sizing and insertion of oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal airways on a simulator.
Explain indications and demonstrate an advanced airway sequence on a simulator, including confirmation and reassessment.
Compare radiography, fluoroscopy, CT, ultrasound, nuclear imaging and MRI by operating principle, hazards and suitability for sample indications.
Elicit relevant allergies, renal status, pregnancy and implanted devices and explain how findings affect imaging selection.
Choose imaging for representative infections, tumours, injuries and congenital conditions across body systems and justify adaptations for children and pregnancy.
Write a simulated requisition with the clinical question and urgency and clarify appropriateness with an imaging specialist.
Distinguish radiation types and compare stochastic effects with tissue reactions, including acute and long-term effects.
Apply time, distance and shielding to a scenario and explain ALARA with reference to applicable AERB guidance.
Explain personal dosimeter use and distinguish commonly reported radiation quantities and units.
Use the official PC-PNDT text to identify its purpose and relevance to simulated primary care.
Use a simulated transfer checklist to verify oxygen, monitoring and MRI compatibility before transport.
Connect anatomy, imaging and pathophysiology in sample osteoarthritis, venous thrombosis and cholecystitis cases.
Identify normal landmarks on chest, abdominal, musculoskeletal and Waters-view films, including the neonatal thymus and paediatric growth plates.
Identify urgent chest, abdominal and skeletal findings including free intraperitoneal air and acute fracture, and distinguish acute from chronic skeletal changes.
Select a suitable reference standard and report a reasoned age range from supplied films.
Assess device position on supplied adult and paediatric ICU chest radiographs and communicate suspected malposition.
Give tailored written and verbal preparation instructions for sample imaging procedures and confirm understanding.
Integrate supplied findings into simulated cases of polycystic ovarian morphology, ectopic pregnancy and infertility.
Explain how supplied findings inform cases of acute or chronic suppurative otitis media and sensorineural hearing loss.
Use supplied imaging to inform simulated decisions in stroke, pulmonary embolism, heart failure and liver parenchymal disease.
Use supplied findings to inform simulated cases of head injury, strangulated hernia, appendicitis and intestinal obstruction.
Explain how supplied findings affect simulated decisions in chest infection, foreign body aspiration and urinary tract infection.
Interpret supplied imaging descriptions in screening and known cancer scenarios and identify the appropriate next diagnostic discussion.
